clue.text: Right to come in to eat, before time's up, where there are no bars?

indicators.note: something coming in to another word is placed inside it

parts.note: to feed is to eat
R is the standard abbreviation for right

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run the opposite way

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Someone asks permission to come indoors for a meal before time runs out, somewhere free of bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a cryptic definition: a place with no prison bars is liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty is the condition of not being locked up behind prison bars, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Musician, a holy one, in devious Merlin's grasp

indicators.note: one item sits in the grasp of the other, placed inside it
a grasp holds something inside, wrapping round it
devious means winding or crooked, so the letters take an indirect route

parts.note: the wizard's name, letters to be rearranged
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A musician who is a saint is held captive by a scheming Merlin.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a medieval singer or player who entertained at court, a kind of musician.

clue.text: Martial epigram, perhaps, is capital

parts.note: martial means to do with war
a saw is an old saying or epigram

explanation.surface: A pithy remark by the Roman poet Martial is judged first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Martial was a Roman writer of epigrams, so the surface reads as literary praise, with 'capital' meaning excellent; here it means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Wise man keeps speaker quiet, seeing the extent of failure

indicators.note: a person who keeps something holds it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
the lip is part of the mouth, the organ one speaks with
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A wise man silences a speaker after realising how badly things have gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippage is the amount by which something falls short of a target, how far a plan has failed.

clue.text: Some current version of Dad after upsetting Mum

indicators.note: upsetting tips something over, so in a down entry the letters turn upside down

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
père is the French version of father

explanation.surface: A modern take on fatherhood emerges after Mum has been upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like modern, but it is electric current; the unit comes after the reversed word for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit measuring electric current, so a quantity of amps is some current.

clue.text: See 22
Maybe first or second row gets spoken about

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: oral means spoken
a row is a noise, a din

explanation.surface: Whether something sits in the front or the next row is being discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a line of seats; here it is a noisy row, said to rhyme with cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers such as first and second give position in a sequence, so these are examples.

clue.text: Upwardly mobile person must be more or less flexible

parts.note: c is short for circa, meaning approximately
limber means supple or flexible

explanation.surface: A social climber has to bend with the times, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' suggests social ambition, and fits that sense, but also covers someone literally going up a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber ascends mountains, and a social climber rises in society, both moving upward.

clue.text: Chaps who have cuppas take to booze in the home counties for a source of power

indicators.note: in places these words inside the region named next

parts.note: the home counties surround London in the South East of England
men who drink tea are tea men
gin is a type of booze

explanation.surface: Tea-drinking men around London switch to the hard stuff to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties around London, in the South East (SE) of England; a cuppa is a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam engine converts heat into mechanical work and powered the Industrial Revolution, a classic source of power.

clue.text: See 22
Spinner and muscleman are ill-balanced

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
a heavy is a strongarm thug

explanation.surface: A spin bowler and a strongman make a lopsided pair.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner suggests a cricket bowler, but here it is a child's spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something top-heavy has too much weight high up, so it is unstable and liable to topple.

clue.text: See 22
22 23 6 12 10? A penny for them

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the linked entries read 'Have you taken leave of your senses?', an exasperated question to someone acting foolishly
second meaning: 'a penny for your thoughts', a gentle question to someone lost in reverie

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references spell out another question, 'Have you taken leave of your senses?'; the answer is a phrase that can say the same thing, and also what you ask when offering a penny for someone's thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: The question works both as an incredulous rebuke of folly and as a polite inquiry into someone's private musings.

clue.text: Gardener's aid to blackbird in fictional village

parts.note: a cloche is a glass or plastic cover protecting young plants
merle is an old or Scots name for the blackbird

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool proves useful against a blackbird in a storybook hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Clochemerle is the 1934 comic novel by Gabriel Chevallier, set in a Beaujolais village of that name feuding over a public urinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clochemerle is the invented French village where Chevallier's satirical novel takes place.

clue.text: Smart boys? Let them stand up before they are counted

definitions.text: Let them stand up before they are counted

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish
Ken is a boy's name, so Kens are boys

explanation.surface: Clever lads are told to rise before a headcount is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'don't count your chickens before they're hatched': let them get on their feet before you count them.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns against counting young poultry before they hatch, so these birds should be up and about first.

clue.text: I had twice left off being refined

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
the word had written two times
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: I had to stop being posh twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had twice' gives I HAD HAD; with L added, all eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-dah describes an affectedly genteel, pretentious manner, a mocking word for over-refined.

clue.text: Bird with a cough that faces work with uncertainty

parts.note: who and that are both relative pronouns
op is short for opus, a work
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A bird with a cold approaches its job hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whooper swan is named for its loud whooping call, which the clue likens to whooping cough.
explanation.definitionFit: The whooper is a large swan whose honking call sounds like the whoop of a bad cough.

clue.text: Covetousness is a bad thing without much art

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the vice wraps around what follows

parts.note: a vice is a bad thing, a moral failing

indicators.note: much of the word art, not all of it, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A moralist declares greed a sin made worse by a lack of culture.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed for wealth, a close synonym of covetousness.

clue.text: See 13
Rugby score disallowed by intervention of a lawman

indicators.note: something that intervenes comes between, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a try is a rugby score; a disallowed one is no try
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby try is ruled out after a legal official steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a try, worth points, is scored by grounding the ball over the opponents' line; the referee may call no try.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a legal officer who certifies documents and oaths, a man of the law.

clue.text: Deprive of money and escape from church

parts.note: to flee is to escape
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone robs the collection and runs away from church.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle or overcharge them, stripping them of cash like shearing a sheep.

clue.text: Every fool has easy avenue to nukes: organiser's sanity is in question

indicators.note: an organiser arranges things, so the letters before are put in a new order

parts.words: Every fool has easy avenue to nukes
parts.note: all twenty-nine letters of the phrase, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Anyone giving every idiot a simple route to nuclear weapons must be out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole long phrase is the fodder; the answer is the question one might put to such an organiser.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking whether someone has lost their wits is a question that doubts their mental soundness.

clue.text: Refugee from alien regime

indicators.note: alien means foreign and strange, so the letters are turned into something unfamiliar

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A refugee fleeing a foreign government.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is someone who has left their country, often for political reasons, much like a refugee.

clue.text: Demeanour of singer captivating audience

indicators.note: captivating takes something captive, holding it inside

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the crooner
an ear is a hearing, an audience, as in 'gain someone's ear'

explanation.surface: A crooner's stage presence charms the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing is the way a person carries and conducts themself, their deportment or demeanour.

clue.text: Nick's not to play without a handicap

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small cut or mark
second meaning: to withdraw from a contest
third meaning: a golfer who plays off zero

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings of one word; 'Nick' with its capital looks like a name, and Old Nick and Old Scratch are both names for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a slight cut, to pull out of an event, and, of a player, having no handicap.
